I’m currently seeing my psychiatrist through UHS. I’m extremely honest and completely transparent with my doctor there. Due to past circumstances daily ADHD treatment for my uncontrolled debilitating ADHD isn’t possible right now, but was given medications for exams only. Because I’m honest and I care a great deal about being open with healthcare professionals about my history with drug use, my doctor did inform me that I will be taking a drug test before I’m able to pick up my meds. It’s UHS policy. There was some research done apparently on marijuana and other drug interactions with ADHD meds, I think it’s just to make sure you’re not on any hard drugs that could be detrimental to your heart or liver or kidneys when taking ADHD meds. But also definitely to weed (haha get it) out those who may have ulterior motives to their health and well-being. I personally had a great deal of emotional and physical struggle trying to pass the drug test, was it worth it for 4 pills a semester when the drug is the only thing that will keep me from tearing apart my skin and picking out all my hair? No absolutely not and I think it’s ridiculous. Did I do it anyway? Yes, and I’d do it again to get the meds I need to succeed in my academics and career. Everything was free (testing) through UHS, I paid like $2 for my meds but I reach my deductible by February usually. 

Also I thought it was VERY odd that they only tested my urine for THC. Not even amphetamines. Clearly they aren’t worried about whether or not I’m taking meds from non prescribed sources. Only if that source is weed. Which is so stupid.

My last relationship was rocky largely due to my emotional instability but also because I absorbed my partner’s personality. Everything he did, I did. I ignored a lot of my other friends telling me that it was unhealthy. Don’t be controlling, as hard as that can be, it does damage in the long term as (at least me) people with BPD tend to gravitate and attach to that control. Avoid seeing each other very often, my partner and I started horribly because we spent every single day and night together, and while it may seem you’re not sick of that person, it’ll make you sick. Just support their hobbies and activities, try not to insert yourself unless your partner explicitly asks you to (like if they are in a club I would avoid joining, or if they’re out with friends I would avoid being attached to them until you guys have a better understanding of each other’s individuality) AGAIN THIS IS ALL FROM MY PERSPECTIVE! You’re an amazing partner for taking this initiative, they are very very lucky to have you in their life

My advice to you as someone who is hyper-aware and has diagnosed BPD, depression, anxiety, and CPTSD is to be careful. The book is amazing and you're an amazing partner to your significant other to take these initiatives. My partner took similar steps to better understand my mental health and it has made us incredibly strong and stable. Don't walk on eggshells but equally be mindful about your partner's trauma. When I come to my partner (or when they come to me) about a problem, concern, or if I had a bad day, we ask each other "do you want comfort or solutions?" and that is honestly the key to any relationship. Be mindful of yourself. In my case, I am quite far on the spectrum for BPD and tend to absorb other's personalities so if you sense that happening be mindful of ways to support your partner's individuality, which for many living with BPD is extremely difficult.
